I've always thought the series tried to mesh strategy with the RPG aspects of leveling and learning about characters. The new feature seems to bring a few things to the table, and I think you have to look at some of it separately.

It's adding greater depth to the character interactions, whether or not you care for it in general or the particular way it's providing it, that portion of it is putting more focus on the "character study" aspect of the series while adding onto the "base" aspect. And I'm talking more about conversations in the barracks, support dialogues, and being able to talk to your units. Not so much the character interaction feature.

It's adding a player housing concept, which should benefit the feeling of importance for the main character. One thing it seems to be focusing on is resource management, which was one of the main criticisms of dropping weapon durability. Depending on how we get these resources, it could be a big deal or it could be a side thing. It's really hard to say how this will turn out, particularly because we don't know much about how we get the resources in the first place. And we can't tell how important that aspect is to the main game.

Finally, and I think this is a big one. It's going to provide a ton of non-main game content. And probably a good amount of end game content as well. I'm really looking forward to the idea of defending the base I've made, or fighting some of these additional challenge teams.

I don't think it's something that isn't in the spirit of the series, which I believe to be a strategy game wrapped in a pretty RPG bow. For me, the question is how much it's going to affect the actual strategy aspect of it, and how well it's going to do so. If done right this could simply provide a great amount of content and choices without diminishing the main game.

My main takeaway from what you said was the word survive, which is how I would describe my early playthroughs. My point is that not everyone will pick up a game as fast, and not everyone is willing to work past the frustration. Adding easier difficulties can benefit newcomers without taking much away, and things like Casual mode are them saving the time of adding another difficulty. Instead of making an even easier mode, they can just add Casual mode and call it a day. If you ask me, Casual mode was a great addition, and I don't think I've ever used it.

Edit: Wow this got long. **TLDR**: I think the new feature can add some cool stuff, I think they've made efforts to add more dynamics to the game and I think the series has a serious learning curve and things like Casual Mode help new players come in without being intimidated.

Your two best projectiles across all variations are a heavy object and an upward attack. Other moves have their uses too, but those two are the most significant. Challenge with the upward attack often (but not when it’s extremely unsafe), and remember you can adjust your aim to target an opponent jumping in or rushing towards you.
